prompt:
Draw a faithful 1440x900 screenshot-style comp of a real desktop benchmark configuration app named BenchForge. New visual world: a logic analyzer workstation, not a website template. Use a cool pale gray-blue background, very dark slate typography, calibrated cyan / teal / muted green / coral channels, sharp thin rules and compact square input fields. Do not use cream, paper, dark terminal, glow, gradients, soft cards, generic dashboard KPI widgets or decorative icons. Layout and palette must differ clearly from a conventional rounded-card SaaS dashboard.

The first viewport is a working “Configure a benchmark” page. A compact wordmark at the top, then a small two-column configuration area. Put setup fields in one tidy left column (about 60% width): Adapter = noop — harness calibration; Scenario choices exactly Normal (selected) and Celebrity; Run settings = 4 workers, 250 ms warm-up, 1000 ms duration, seed 42; Synthetic ID space = 10,000 users, 100,000 posts, 200,000 follows, 1,000 hashtags. Put a narrow Recent runs list to the right, with “No runs yet”, no sample rows and no charts.

The lower half of the main column is the signature instrument: six horizontal flat logic lanes aligned to one ruler from 0% to 100%; each lane visibly labeled and filled exactly to its weight: Timeline read 40, Profile read 25, Post like 15, Post create 10, Hashtag search 5, Follow 5. Total 100%. This encodes the form's configured percentages only, never performance or live telemetry. Place a modest “Start run” control directly beneath these lanes. Show “Synthetic workload. No social app data.” and a readable note that noop does not connect to a database and results measure harness overhead only. No extra scenarios, adapters, features, run records, success claims, latency/throughput numbers, fake data, or social content. Clear readable UI text, semantic labels, precise numerical alignment.
